oewn-00811126-n.learner: the act of owning something and having control over it
examples: a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife
you may take possession of Longbourn estate whenever it falls

oewn-00032912-n.learner: a thing that someone owns or has
examples: She packed her few possessions into one small bag.

oewn-14431199-n.learner: the state of being controlled by a strong feeling or by a spirit
examples: The villagers spoke of her fits as a case of demonic possession.
the cheeks of each were overspread with the deepest blush

oewn-00693335-a.learner: reaching a long way down from the top, or a long way in from the outside, the back, the side, or the centre
examples: The water in the middle of the lake is very deep.

oewn-01515033-s.learner: very strong, or reaching an extreme
examples: such an assurance of the deepest disgrace

oewn-01879131-s.learner: showing thinking that goes far below the surface
examples: For you are a young lady of deep reflection, I know, and read great books

connotation.why: credits the thinker rather than only describing the thought

oewn-00617843-v.learner: to fail to look after or deal with someone or something
examples: Without a governess, you must have been neglected.

connotation.why: faults the person for care that was not given

oewn-00616690-v.learner: to leave something undone, or to leave it out
examples: I am sure you neglect nothing that can add to the beauties of that noble place.

oewn-00618547-v.learner: to give little attention or no attention to someone or something
examples: I was sure you loved your girls too well to neglect such an acquaintance.

oewn-02362227-v.learner: to spend very little, and to avoid wasting what you have
examples: Your profusion makes me saving.
If she is half as sharp as her mother, she is saving enough.

oewn-02556565-v.learner: to keep someone or something from being ruined, destroyed, or harmed
examples: This was a lucky recollection--it saved her from something like regret.

oewn-00550632-v.learner: to make some spending or some effort no longer needed
examples: It will save me a world of trouble and economy.

oewn-02230274-v.learner: to keep something and set it aside for your own use or for a special use
examples: he will be vastly happy to oblige you, and will save all the best of the coveys for you

oewn-01347791-v.learner: to move something so that an opening or a way through is blocked; to shut it
examples: the door was on the point of being closed

oewn-02430760-v.learner: to bring a meeting, a speech, or something like it to an end
examples: I have been making the tour of the park, and intended to close it with a call at the Parsonage.
he was angry that the ball closed so early

oewn-01778057-v.learner: to dislike someone or something very strongly, or to feel a deep unwillingness towards them
examples: I hate such false friends.
She certainly did not hate him.

oewn-90017091-v.learner: to feel bad things about a person and to say them out loud
examples: They hate the new mayor and say so at every meeting.

oewn-00486999-r.learner: in a way that goes well beyond what is usual
examples: there are several of them, you see, uncommonly pretty
You write uncommonly fast.

oewn-02433334-v.learner: to leave a meeting or a gathering of people
examples: With proper civilities, the ladies then withdrew.

oewn-01998474-v.learner: to move back or away from where you were
examples: The army withdrew to the far side of the river.

oewn-00801045-v.learner: to pull out of something you had promised to do or had already begun
examples: He withdrew from the race a week before the vote.

oewn-02197640-v.learner: to notice something with your eyes, ears, or other senses
examples: On distinguishing the ladies of the group the two gentlemen came directly towards them

oewn-00924409-v.learner: to make someone or something stand out as worth noticing
examples: Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters.
with no further attempt to distinguish Elizabeth

connotation.why: singles the person out as deserving the notice

oewn-00652006-v.learner: to mark things off from each other as being different
examples: Lawyers distinguish two kinds of contract in this section.

oewn-01763170-v.learner: to bring out a feeling or a reaction in someone
examples: an evening which had raised such splendid expectations
this poor man cannot come to a house without raising all this speculation

oewn-01978076-v.learner: to move something from a lower place to a higher one
examples: Mr. Bennet raised his eyes from his book as she entered
He was writing, and, without raising his head, coolly replied

oewn-00545629-v.learner: to move someone up to a higher rank or a better condition
examples: Wealth raised the family from poverty to comfort.
